# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/security_functions.md
# The E2E server uses the identity from the documented example.
SELECT SESSION_USER()
=> "jdoe@example.com"

SELECT TYPEOF(SESSION_USER())
=> "STRING"

CREATE TEMP FUNCTION Identity() AS (SESSION_USER());
SELECT Identity()
=> "jdoe@example.com"

DECLARE identity STRING DEFAULT SESSION_USER();
SELECT identity
=> "jdoe@example.com"

SELECT SESSION_USER();
SELECT SESSION_USER()
=> "jdoe@example.com"

# The documented signature takes no arguments.
SELECT SESSION_USER('jdoe@example.com')
=> error:

# Verified against BigQuery by a maintainer: SAFE. is rejected for SESSION_USER, even where
# TYPEOF does not evaluate its argument.
SELECT SAFE.SESSION_USER() IS NOT NULL
=> error: SAFE with function session_user is not supported.

SELECT TYPEOF(SAFE.SESSION_USER())
=> error: SAFE with function session_user is not supported.

DECLARE identity STRING DEFAULT SAFE.SESSION_USER();
SELECT identity
=> error:

# Observed BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers. SECURE_CONTEXT is
# recognized but cannot run in a standalone SELECT.
SELECT SECURE_CONTEXT('bq_emulator_unverified_key')
=> error: SECURE_CONTEXT() is only supported inside logical view definitions or row access policy definitions.

SELECT SECURE_CONTEXT('')
=> error: SECURE_CONTEXT() is only supported inside logical view definitions or row access policy definitions.

SELECT SECURE_CONTEXT(CAST(NULL AS STRING))
=> error contains: The argument to SECURE_CONTEXT must be non-NULL

SELECT SECURE_CONTEXT(123)
=> error contains: Argument 1: Unable to coerce type INT64 to expected type STRING

SELECT SAFE.SECURE_CONTEXT('bq_emulator_unverified_key')
=> error contains: Function SECURE_CONTEXT does not support SAFE error mode
